To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of a leverage correction to the PRESS statistic for model validation and selection in calibration models built with PCR and PLS can be justified.

1) PLS is the method of choice for spectroscopy calibration, because it has a lower prediction variance and is therefore less sensitive to noise than PCR; 2) the PRESS statistic is the most reliable criterion for model optimization, and 3) the leverage correction is an effective way to approximate the PRESS statistic.
The use of a PLS regression model with a large number of components is not necessarily a good idea, and the use of a PPLS regression model with a single component is not necessarily a bad one.

the development of a new approach to calibration modeling and its optimization for spectroscopic data analysis.
